_provenance.purpose: Test whether Lidl and Aldi Nord can supply (a) a machine-readable store locator and (b) a grocery price catalog. Resolves open questions 1 and 2 in docs/research/location-and-travel-feasibility.md.
_provenance.method: 9 HTTP GETs total, all to paths advertised in lidl.de's own robots.txt sitemap, plus the store-detail URLs derived from that sitemap. curl only. No JavaScript executed, no headless browser, no authentication, no CAPTCHA handling, no bot-protection circumvention.

paths_deliberately_NOT_requested: /user-api/* (Disallow) - the per-user/store context API. Off-limits; NOT probed. This is almost certainly the path that resolves an InStoreOnly price once a store is selected, so it was NOT used.
/cqe/* (Disallow) - the price/query backend. Off-limits; NOT probed.

_provenance.extraction_path: product: script[application/ld+json] -> @type=='Product'. stores: city page HTML -> a.store-tile-detail-page__link[href] + its aria-label attribute.
_provenance.raw_artefact_policy: The full sitemaps (1.4 MB product, 853 KB store) and retailer page HTML are copyrighted and bulky, so per the convention in data/raw/spike/README.md they are NOT committed. This file records the factual fields, the extraction rule, and sha256 digests so any finding can be re-verified.

sitemap_index.note: The product sitemap path is /p/export/DE/de/... i.e. market-scoped. de-AT and de-CH equivalents are implied by the store sitemap's hreflang alternates but were NOT fetched.

product_sitemap.count_caveat: This count was already recorded in the original spike (lidl_observed.json -> product_discovery.product_url_count = 13337). It is re-confirmed here, NOT a new figure.

catalog_composition.headline: The advertised product catalog is a general-merchandise and alcohol catalog, not a grocery catalog. Genuine groceries are a negligible minority.
catalog_composition.method: Leading slug token classified as the product's own-brand family, then hand-mapped. Whole-token matching, not substring matching, to avoid false positives.
catalog_composition.non_food_share_of_top_15_brands: roughly 7300 of 13337 (~55%) from the top non-food own-brand families alone, before counting alcohol, third-party brands, clothing, baby, beauty and garden
catalog_composition.known_false_positive_warning: The slug token 'brot' is NOT reliable for bread. 'silvercrest-brot-frischhaltedose' (p100409619) is a bread-freshness STORAGE CONTAINER, a 9.99 EUR non-food item. Any grocery classifier built on slug substrings will produce silent false positives like this.

grocery_price_availability.headline: Real grocery products return NO price and NO GTIN in server-rendered HTML. The price-bearing pages are the non-food/alcohol webshop range.

tested.interpretation: A genuine grocery. No price, no GTIN in server HTML. Offer availability is InStoreOnly, i.e. Lidl only reveals a price after a store is selected.
A NON-food item (storage box) that nonetheless carries price + 2 GTINs. Demonstrates the GTIN and price fields are real and parseable, but only populated for the OnlineOnly range.

grocery_price_availability.derived_rule: OnlineOnly => price and GTIN present in server HTML. InStoreOnly => price is null and no GTIN. Lidl's actual grocery range is InStoreOnly.
grocery_price_availability.consequence: Obtaining a real Lidl grocery price appears to require the store-selection flow, which resolves through /user-api/* and /cqe/*. BOTH ARE DISALLOW-ED IN robots.txt and were therefore NOT probed. This is a hard stop under our constraints, not an obstacle to engineer around.
grocery_price_availability.status: CONCLUSIVE - do not invest further in Lidl as a price source

store_locator.headline: SOLVED for Lidl. City pages yield exact store -> street + postcode + city mappings, server-rendered and machine-readable. No coordinates, but postcodes are enough to join the PLZ centroid dataset.

store_sitemap.coverage_caveat: Coverage is UNEVEN. /filialen/berlin/ exists as a city page but has ZERO store-detail URLs in the sitemap, whereas /filialen/rostock/ has many. The sitemap therefore must not be assumed to be a complete store registry.

store_locator.extraction_rule: On a city page, each store is one anchor: <a href="/s/de-DE/filialen/{city}/{street}/" aria-label="Lidl Filiale {street}, {PLZ} {city}" class="store-tile-detail-page__link">

conclusions_for_the_project: Lidl is RULED OUT as a price source. Its advertised catalog is ~99% non-food and alcohol, and its real grocery prices are only reachable through robots-disallowed endpoints.

Store locators are now SOLVED for 2 of 6 chains. Lidl gives postcode via city pages; Aldi Nord gives lat/lng + postcode + opening hours + regional banner via store pages. Neither needs an external gazetteer.
The per-banner assortment question is ANSWERED for Aldi Nord: each store names its own Regionalgesellschaft in openingHoursNotes, so banner-level modelling is derivable from the locator payload.
Coordinates being real store positions rather than postcode centroids is a genuine accuracy win for the travel-cost model, and it is the strongest argument so far for the total-cost framing.
The price side remains the binding constraint at 1 of 6 chains, and it is now known to be a data-availability wall rather than a scraping-difficulty wall.

aldi_nord_store_page.headline: SOLVED for Aldi Nord too, and better than Lidl. Store pages expose lat/lng, postcode, opening hours AND the regional banner (Regionalgesellschaft) in one server-rendered payload. The postcode that is missing from Aldi's sitemap IS on the store page.

probes.note: no city index page exists; Aldi has no Lidl-style city listing route

aldi_nord_store_page.extraction_rule: __NEXT_DATA__ script -> props.pageProps.storeDetail (a JS-string-escaped JSON object nested inside a stringified payload; it must be un-escaped and brace-balanced before json.loads). The same object is NOT exposed as application/ld+json: the page has 8 ld+json blocks but none is a Store/LocalBusiness entity.

observed_store_detail_fields.name: ALDI Nord
observed_store_detail_fields.openingHoursNotes: Regionalgesellschaft: ALDI GmbH & Co. Kommanditgesellschaft, Anklamer Str. 9, 17126 Jarmen
observed_store_detail_fields.photos: list with publicUrl, served from locator.uberall.com

three_findings.postcode_present: VERIFIED. zip='18119' on the store page, absent from the sitemap URL. Combined with the city+street slug in the sitemap this is a complete store->postcode mapping, so Aldi needs no external gazetteer either.
three_findings.coordinates_present: VERIFIED. lat/lng are exact store coordinates, not postcode centroids. Cross-checked against the plz_geocoord file: the Lortzingstr. store sits 0.56 km from the 18119 centroid, and 2.2-10.9 km from the neighbouring Rostock centroids it was compared against. This is materially better than centroid-based placement, because a postcode centroid in a city like Rostock can be kilometres from the shop.
three_findings.banner_present: VERIFIED, and this closes open question 2. openingHoursNotes names the operating Regionalgesellschaft (here ALDI GmbH & Co. Kommanditgesellschaft, Jarmen). A store therefore identifies its own legal entity and, by extension, its regional assortment. Banner-level assortment modelling is answerable from the locator payload without any additional source.

aldi_nord_store_page.important_negative: There is NO city index page for Aldi Nord (/filialen-und-oeffnungszeiten/rostock.html is 404). Enumeration must therefore come from the advertised store sitemap, not from a crawl of city pages. This is the structural difference from Lidl, whose city pages are the reliable enumeration route.
